text:
ashok: alerting — production cache miss rate jumped from ~2% to ~67% at 12:12 UTC after the v2-opt canary. latency + backend QPS spiked. tagging eng-sre and eng-runtime. anyone oncall?

sre-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-045. Pager duty routed to @oliver. Metrics dashboard: https://dash.redwood/INC-2026-045 :rotating_light:

oliver: I see the spike. Cache service (prefix-kv) RPC error rate up ~3x and origin request QPS doubled. Trying to look at the keys driving the misses.

maria: grabbing profiler traces from the runtime. early notes: kernel selection still OK, but the KV cache hit metric (prefix_cache.hit_rate) dropped to 0.31. I can export a sample of keys.

devon: quick question — did we change any cache keying in the deploy? or was it purely model binary?

ashok: only change in the canary was model v2-opt + a tokenizer tweak (to align BPE with training). no cache code changes in the release.

maria: uploaded short dump — sample keys show tokenized-prefix hashes. interestingly identical textual prompts have different token sequences under v2 tokenizer. example:

```
# Example prompt
"Summarize: The quarterly roadmap..."
# v1 tokens -> [1002, 45, 77,...]
# v2 tokens -> [1002, 46, 77,...]
```

maria: because our cache keys currently include the tokenized prefix length/ids (for faster KV matching), tokenization drift means same text -> different cache key -> cache miss.

samira: ugh. that explains sudden miss storm. Backend got hammered because every request missed and fallback fetched full model KV cache (expensive).

oliver: mitigation — can we flip the cache keying to raw-text normalized key quickly via feature flag? That should make v1/v2 share keys.

ashok: we have a runtime flag `enable_text_keying` but it's gated behind config rollout. We can flip on canary hosts now and monitor. doing it for 20% first.

deploy-bot: Rollout started: enable_text_keying -> 20% (eng-runtime-canary).

maria: after toggling on 20%: global hit_rate marginally better in those hosts. but overall still low because many hosts still use token-keying.

devon: we should also add jitter to cache TTL and singleflight/coalesce for concurrent misses to avoid stampedes. current behaviour: no leader election per key. if 100 requests for same new prefix arrive, we fan out to origin 100x.

oliver: yes — implement singleflight for prefix loads (in-process) and a small distributed lock for multi-host. short-term we can rate-limit origin backfills with a leaky-bucket per-prefix.

maria: profiling shows a secondary cause: batching heuristics were bumped to prefer larger batch sizes at low concurrency in v2. That increased per-request latency for cache population because backfill loads are larger and slower, exacerbating throttling.

samira: action list for now: 1) finish flipping enable_text_keying to 100% across canaries (ashok), 2) enable in-process singleflight on all hosts (maria) as emergency toggle, 3) throttle backfill QPS per-prefix at gateway (devon), 4) rollback tokenizer change if needed (ashok).

ashok: done — text keying at 100% across canaries. monitoring now.

maria: singleflight toggle ON on runtime group A. initial results: hosts with singleflight show ~8x reduction in origin backfill QPS for hot prefixes.

oliver: backend QPS and latency trending back to baseline. marking incident as mitigated. will remain in response mode until stable for 2 hours.

devon: postmortem notes / followups:
- stop keying by token ids; move to stable normalized textual keys (strip whitespace, lowercase, canonical unicode).
- add per-prefix singleflight with short lease + fallback jitter.
- implement small randomized TTL jitter (10-20%) to avoid synchronized expirations.
- add cache_key_tokenizer_version metric (so future tokenization changes surface as key entropy spikes).
- add canary warmup job: on model rollout, kickoff background prefix warmups for top 1k prefixes to avoid cold-start storm.
- audit batching heuristics interplay with cache warmups; add a throttle to backfill batch size.

samira: agree. also recommend adding an alarm: cache_miss_rate > 20% AND origin_qps_delta > 2x -> auto-disable token-keying or trigger singleflight.

ashok: I'll open a PR with the keying change and a RFC for warmup + singleflight (linked in incident ticket).

maria: curious note for ML team — tokenizer drift is a valid backward-incompatibility for runtime caching. ask models to include tokenizer compatibility tag for serving.

oliver: closing loop: INC-2026-045 -> mitigated; postmortem draft assigned to @maria. thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
